authoredSolutions.64: For \(2\times2\) with \(t=\mathrm{tr}A,d=\det A=-1\): \(\det(A+I)=1+t+d=t\) and \(\det(\mathrm{adj}A+I)=t\). So \(t^2=4\Rightarrow t=\pm2\); \(2\) is available.
authoredSolutions.67: Numerator \(=\ln((1+x^2)^2-x^2)=\ln(1+x^2+x^4)\sim x^2\); denominator \(=\sec x-\cos x=\sin^2x/\cos x\sim x^2\). Limit \(k=1\).

authoredSolutions.72: Locus: \(x^2+y^2+x-3y-2=0\). x-axis chord \(AB=3\) (roots \(-2,1\)); y-axis chord \(CD=\sqrt{17}\). Diagonals perpendicular: area \(=\tfrac12\cdot3\cdot\sqrt{17}=\tfrac{3\sqrt{17}}{2}\).

authoredSolutions.77: Each \(P\in[0,1]\) and sum \(\le1\): \((26-3p)/24\le1\Rightarrow p\ge\tfrac23\); \(P(E_3)\ge0\Rightarrow p\le1\). So \(p\in[\tfrac23,1]\), \(p_1+p_2=1+\tfrac23=\tfrac53\).
authoredSolutions.80: Truth table: \((\sim(p\Leftrightarrow\sim q))\wedge q\) is true only at \(p=T,q=T\), identical to \((p\Rightarrow q)\wedge p\).
authoredSolutions.81: Disc \(=-4(pr-q^2)^2\le0\Rightarrow pr=q^2\), double root \(=q/p=t\in\{2,-4\}\). \((q^2+r^2)/p^2=t^2+t^4\). \(t=2\Rightarrow p,q,r\) same sign (excluded); \(t=-4\Rightarrow16+256=272\).
authoredSolutions.83: Set \(n\) ends at the \(n^2\)-th multiple of 3 and has \(2n-1\) terms. 11th set: multiples indexed \(101\ldots121\). Sum \(=3\sum_{m=101}^{121}m=3\cdot\tfrac{(101+121)\cdot21}{2}=3\cdot2331=6993\).
authoredSolutions.84: Expand: \(x^8-x^7-x^6+x^5+3x^4-4x^3-2x^2+4x-1\). Sign analysis gives simple roots at \(x=-1\) and \(x\approx0.4\), and a double (touch) root at \(x=1\). Distinct real roots \(=3\).
authoredSolutions.87: \(\int_3^x y\,dx=(y/x)^3\); differentiate with \(u=y/x\Rightarrow u\,u'=x/3\Rightarrow u^2=x^2/3-2\), so \(y^2=x^4/3-2x^2\). \(y=6\sqrt{10}\Rightarrow\alpha^4/3-2\alpha^2=360\Rightarrow\alpha^2=36,\ \alpha=6\).

authoredSolutions.89: \(f'=4x-1/x=0\Rightarrow a=\tfrac12\), parabola \(y^2=2x\). Tangent \(ty=x+t^2/2\) through \((4,3)\Rightarrow t^2-6t+8=0\); \(t=2\) passes \((-2,0)\) (excluded), so \(t=4\), \(P=(8,4)\). Normal \(4x+y=36\Rightarrow x/9+y/36=1\), \(\alpha+\beta=45\).
authoredSolutions.151: \(x^2+(3-a)x+(1-2a)=0\): sum \(S=a-3\), product \(P=1-2a\). Sum of squares of roots \(=S^2-2P=(a-3)^2-2(1-2a)=a^2-2a+7\), minimized at \(a=1\) giving \(6\).
authoredSolutions.152: \(|z-i|=|z+5i|\) is the perpendicular bisector of \((0,1)\) and \((0,-5)\), i.e. \(y=-2\). With \(|z|=2\): \(x^2+4=4\Rightarrow x=0\). So \(z=-2i\), which satisfies \(x+2y+4=0\).
authoredSolutions.154: \(\sum_{i,j}{}^nC_i{}^nC_j=(2^n)^2=2^{2n}\); the diagonal \(\sum_i({}^nC_i)^2={}^{2n}C_n\). Hence the \(i\neq j\) sum \(=2^{2n}-{}^{2n}C_n\).
authoredSolutions.155: Minimize distance from centre \((1,-1)\) to \((t,t^2)\): \(2t^3+3t-1=0\Rightarrow t\approx0.31\), \(Q\approx(0.31,0.10)\). \(P\) is on segment \(CQ\) at unit distance from \(C\); its abscissa \(\approx0.47\in(1/4,1/2)\).
authoredSolutions.156: \(f'(x)=\frac{2}{1+4x^2}-3a\ge0\) on the interval requires \(3a\le\frac{2}{1+4(\pi/6)^2}=\frac{18}{9+\pi^2}\), so \(\bar a=\frac{6}{9+\pi^2}\). Then \(3\bar a\cdot\frac{\pi}{8}=\frac{9\pi}{4(9+\pi^2)}\), giving \(f_{\bar a}(\pi/8)=8-\frac{9\pi}{4(9+\pi^2)}\).
authoredSolutions.157: \(e^{3x}-1=3x+\frac{9x^2}{2}+\cdots\). Numerator \((\alpha-3)x-\frac{9x^2}{2}\); denominator \(\sim3\alpha x^2\). Finite limit needs \(\alpha=3\), then \(\beta=\frac{-9/2}{9}=-\frac12\). \(\alpha+\beta=\frac52\).
authoredSolutions.158: \(\log_{\cos x}\csc x=\frac{-\ln\sin x}{\ln\cos x}\). At \(x=\pi/4\), differentiating gives \(\frac{d}{dx}=\frac{4}{\ln2}\). Thus \(\ln2\cdot\frac{4}{\ln2}=4\).
authoredSolutions.159: \((|\sin x|+|\cos x|)^2=1+|\sin2x|\). \(\int_0^{20\pi}(1+|\sin2x|)dx=20\pi+40=20(\pi+2)\) (each of the 40 half-periods of \(|\sin2x|\) contributes 1).
authoredSolutions.160: IF \(=\sqrt{1-x^2}\); \(\frac{d}{dx}(y\sqrt{1-x^2})=x^4+2x\Rightarrow y\sqrt{1-x^2}=\frac{x^5}{5}+x^2\) (through origin). Odd term vanishes; \(\int_{-\sqrt3/2}^{\sqrt3/2}\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}dx=\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\).
authoredSolutions.162: Tangent to \(y=x^2\): \(y=2tx-t^2\). Tangency to \(y=-(x-2)^2\) needs discriminant 0: \(8t^2-16t=0\Rightarrow t=0\) or \(t=2\). \(t=2\) gives \(y=4x-4=4(x-1)\).
authoredSolutions.163: Centre = midpoint \((2,-1)\Rightarrow a=-2,b=1\). Diameter form gives \(x^2+y^2-4x+2y+(-6-7)=0\Rightarrow c=-13\). \(a+b-c=-2+1+13=12\).

authoredSolutions.172: Plane through \((1,1,0)\) with normal \(d_1\times d_2=(1-a^2,a+1,a+1)\). Distance from \((2,1,4)=\frac{|5-a|}{\sqrt{(1-a)^2+2}}=\sqrt3\Rightarrow a^2+2a-8=0\Rightarrow a=2\) or \(-4\); largest is \(2\).
